slides.title: Wind-driven surface circulation
slides.body:
**Surface currents** are driven primarily by wind stress, modified by Earth's rotation (Coriolis effect):

• **Equator** (0° lat): no Coriolis → wind stress directly drives surface currents (Equatorial Currents).
• **Mid-latitudes** (30°): Coriolis deflects flow ~45° right of wind in Northern Hemisphere (left in S). Ekman transport (depth-averaged) is 90° to right.
• **Subtropical gyres** (30°N + 30°S): wind stress curl drives clockwise circulation (NH; CCW in SH). Gulf Stream (W. Atlantic), Kuroshio (W. Pacific), Brazil + Agulhas Currents on western boundaries — fast + narrow (~50 km wide, 1-2 m/s).
• **Subpolar gyres** (60°): cyclonic; Labrador + Norwegian Currents.
• **Antarctic Circumpolar Current (ACC)**: only current that circles globe; ~125 Sv (1 Sv = 10⁶ m³/s).

**Western boundary intensification** (Stommel 1948): wind-stress curl from trade winds + westerlies, combined with Coriolis variation with latitude (β-effect), forces gyres' return flow into intense narrow western boundary currents. Gulf Stream peaks at 100 Sv off Cape Hatteras.

**Ekman spiral + transport**: wind drives surface layer 45° from wind direction; each successive layer rotates slightly more + slower. Net depth-integrated Ekman transport is 90° from wind. Drives **upwelling** at coasts where Ekman transport pushes water offshore (California, Peru, Benguela coasts) — nutrient-rich → productive fisheries.

slides.title: Geostrophic balance + thermal wind
slides.body:
Away from boundaries + over time scales > a day, ocean currents are in **geostrophic balance**: pressure gradient force balances Coriolis. 

  f × v_geo = (1/ρ) ∇P

In the open ocean: currents flow along sea-surface-height contours (high SSH to the right in NH). Satellite altimetry (TOPEX/Poseidon, Jason series) measures SSH to ±2 cm → maps geostrophic currents.

**Thermal wind balance** (combination of geostrophic + hydrostatic): 

  ∂v/∂z = (g / f ρ_0) × ∂ρ/∂x

Vertical current shear is set by horizontal density gradients. So mapping ocean density (T + S vs depth) lets us infer currents from depth profiles — used since Sverdrup era.

**Sverdrup transport**: meridional transport across mid-ocean ≈ wind stress curl / β × f. Predicts gyre interior; western boundary currents close the budget.

slides.title: Thermohaline circulation + AMOC
slides.body:
**Thermohaline circulation (THC)** is the deep, density-driven 'global conveyor belt':

1. North Atlantic: surface water cools + sinks (NADW formation, ~15 Sv).
2. NADW flows southward at ~2-4 km depth along Atlantic deep western boundary.
3. Joins Antarctic Circumpolar Current; mixes with AABW (forms in Weddell + Ross Seas, ~8-10 Sv).
4. Upwells diffusely across Indian + Pacific Oceans (slow, ~25-50 m/yr) + intensely near ACC.
5. Surface return flow back to N. Atlantic via Indonesian Throughflow, Agulhas leakage, Gulf Stream system.

Round-trip time: ~1000-2000 years.

**Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation (AMOC)**: specifically the Atlantic part. Transports ~1.3 PW (10¹⁵ W) heat northward — comparable to atmospheric meridional heat transport at 30°N. Northwest Europe is 5-10 °C warmer than equivalent latitudes in NA because of AMOC heat transport.

**Climate-change concerns**:
• Increased freshwater input (Greenland ice melt + Arctic precipitation) reduces N. Atlantic surface salinity → weakens NADW formation.
• Direct observations (RAPID array since 2004): AMOC has decreased ~15% since 1950s; ~3 Sv weakening detected.
• Tipping point: full AMOC collapse possible if forcing exceeds threshold. Last collapse: ~12.9 kyr ago (Younger Dryas), N. hemisphere cooled 5-10 °C in decades.
• IPCC AR6: high confidence in AMOC weakening this century; low confidence in collapse before 2100.
• Consequences if collapse: drastic NW Europe cooling, tropical rainfall shifts, ocean carbon uptake declines.

question.question: Compute Ekman transport for coastal upwelling
question.goal: California coast: 35°N. Equatorward wind stress τ = 0.1 Pa during summer. Estimate Ekman transport + the upwelling that results.

steps.prompt: Compute Coriolis parameter at 35°N. f = 2 Ω sin φ, Ω = 7.27×10⁻⁵ rad/s.
Compute Ekman transport per unit length of coast: M_E = τ / (ρ_0 × f). ρ_0 ≈ 1025 kg/m³.
steps.reveal: M_E = 0.1 / (1025 × 8.34×10⁻⁵) ≈ 1.17 m²/s. Net transport directed 90° to the right of wind in NH — so equatorward wind drives transport offshore (westward off California). Surface water flows offshore; replacement water upwells from below.

steps.prompt: If this Ekman transport persists over a coast 1000 km long, what's the volume transport in Sv?
steps.reveal: 1.17 Sv (~1.17 million m³/s) offshore Ekman transport along the California coast. Replacement: deep cold nutrient-rich water upwells — sets up the productive California Current ecosystem (sardines, anchovies, plankton blooms, fisheries).

acceptedAnswers: wind weakens → less upwelling → SST rises → ecosystem collapse

steps.reveal: El Niño weakens equatorial trade winds + the South American coastal upwelling that normally drives high productivity. Warm surface waters persist; thermocline deepens; cold nutrient-rich water can't reach surface. Anchovy populations collapse; bird + marine-mammal die-offs (Peru); fish stocks fail. Ripple effects: tropical Pacific precipitation shifts (drought in Australia, floods in South America); global temperature spike (El Niño years are typically global-temperature records). Inter-annual ENSO oscillation drives much of global climate variability.

question.question: Order these ocean circulation cells by their *typical residence time / overturning timescale* (fastest to slowest).

items.label: AMOC upper limb (Gulf Stream → NADW formation)

question.explanation: Timescales: Mixed layer mixing ~days-weeks (wind-driven turbulent mixing). Subtropical gyres ~years-decade (~1000s of km, m/s currents). ACC overturning ~decades to century. AMOC upper limb ~50-100 years. Global thermohaline conveyor ~1000-2000 years (ages of deep water as measured by ¹⁴C). This wide separation of timescales (days to millennia) means ocean circulation has nested 'memory' — surface forcing is felt immediately + atmospheric weather, but deep ocean carries climate signals from centuries past. Climate models must capture all scales.

question.question: Why is Northwest Europe (e.g., London, 51°N) ~5-10 °C warmer in winter than equivalent latitudes in N. America (e.g., Labrador, 51°N)?
options: The North Atlantic AMOC transports ~1.3 PW of heat northward — warm Gulf Stream + Norwegian Current waters carry tropical heat to NW Europe. Without AMOC, NW Europe would be 5-10 °C colder, similar to Labrador (which is in the cold Labrador Current path). Additionally, prevailing westerly winds pick up heat + moisture from the warm ocean + deliver it to Europe.
Solar heating differs between continents at the same latitude.
question.explanation:
**NW Europe warming sources**:

1. **AMOC heat transport**: ~1.3 PW (1.3 × 10¹⁵ W) of meridional ocean heat transport across 30°N. Roughly half of the heat that *should* be transported by atmospheric circulation alone (Hadley + Ferrel cells). Concentrated in NA + NW Europe due to Atlantic basin geometry.
2. **Gulf Stream + North Atlantic Drift**: warm surface waters from tropical/subtropical Atlantic carry heat poleward.
3. **Norwegian Atlantic Current**: extends into Nordic Seas, keeping ports ice-free year-round (Murmansk, Bergen).
4. **Westerly winds** transport heat + moisture from the warm ocean to the European landmass — pre-warmed air.

**Comparison N. America at same latitude**:
- Labrador Current: cold + flowing southward along NA east coast.
- Polar continental air masses unmodified by warm water (no eastward warm-current intermediary).
- Result: 50-51°N in NA = -20 to -30 °C winters in interior; 50-51°N in NW Europe = 0-5 °C winters.

**AMOC weakening scenario**:
- Direct cooling: 2-5 °C drop in NW Europe over decades.
- Indirect: storm-track shifts; precipitation reorganization; agriculture + infrastructure impacts.
- Probabilistic risk: IPCC AR6 says full collapse 'very unlikely' before 2100, but not negligible (some studies suggest 10-20% probability of collapse in 21st century). Beyond 2100: high uncertainty.
- 'AMOC tipping' is one of the most-studied climate tipping points; would have global consequences (also tropical rainfall shifts, ocean carbon uptake decline, sea-level redistribution).

Research: RAPID array (mooring across 26.5°N) measures AMOC since 2004; 15% decrease detected. Reconstructions from ocean sediments suggest AMOC at multi-millennium low in 21st century — concerning trajectory.

hints: What heat transport mechanism is at work?
Compare to Labrador at same latitude.
slides.workedSolution: AMOC transports ~1.3 PW heat northward via Gulf Stream + N. Atlantic Drift + Norwegian Atlantic Current. NW Europe receives this heat + westerly winds redistribute it inland. N. America at same latitude sees cold Labrador Current + polar continental air — 5-10 °C colder. AMOC collapse would cool NW Europe substantially. RAPID array detects 15% AMOC weakening since 2004; IPCC views full collapse before 2100 as 'very unlikely' but possible.

question.prompt: In ≤120 words, explain how the ocean's global circulation acts as a 'climate flywheel' — buffering atmospheric variability but also transmitting climate signals across centuries.
question.rubric: Mentions: ocean heat capacity ~1000× atmospheric per unit volume; >90% of recent global warming has gone into the ocean. Surface ocean responds to atmospheric forcing on weeks-decade. Deep ocean responds on centuries-millennia. Heat + carbon stored in deep ocean buffers atmospheric anomalies but releases slowly. Climate-change implication: even if emissions stopped today, deep ocean would continue adjusting for centuries (committed warming, sea-level rise). Climate-natural-variability: ENSO, AMOC, PDO oscillations transmit climate signals on years-to-centuries timescales. Conclusion: ocean simultaneously stabilizes climate (huge heat capacity) + introduces multi-decadal/centennial variability. Modern climate science treats ocean + atmosphere as a coupled system; can't model one without the other.
